issues.note: Real lumping of instrument and achievement uses, but the definition is usable.
Implies tape predates record, which is false; it is also a history claim.
Record means an album in any format; restricting it to vinyl misleads learners.
Stress is stated in four fields; it also correctly notes the IPA contradiction.
One takes a photo; record a photo is unnatural.
House ruling 16: participle phrases are phrase collocations.
The verb is rɪˈkɔrd; noun stress given, contradicting the notes.
The stress fact is duplicated across the notes fields.
Same participle-phrase typing error in sense 2.
Names a concrete three-way split, so it is not wholly generic; small point.
It mostly restates the grammar values and patterns, against notes discipline.
Take is a light verb, not a synonym of record.
The duplicate collocation is a real small point; lumping is arguable.

findings.F1: The tape-v compare note falsely calls tape the older word and makes a history claim outside the etymology field.
findings.F2: The usage note wrongly limits the noun record to vinyl discs; it also covers albums in any format.
findings.F3: Verb and noun stress is stated in several fields (pronunciation notes, usage note, adaptation, word family).
findings.F4: The collocation 'record a photo' is unnatural; one takes a photo.
findings.F5: Sense 1 participle phrases are typed adverb + verb instead of phrase.
findings.F6: The American IPA gives the noun stress ˈrɛk.ɚd instead of the verb's rɪˈkɔrd.
findings.F7: Sense 2 participle phrases are typed adverb + verb instead of phrase.
findings.F8: The grammar adaptation note only restates the sense grammar fields.
findings.F9: take-v is listed as a synonym of record though it is only a light-verb partner.
